body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-09. Reported by the CWNG KOBO session after it bit them; verified
here in the source before filing.

scripts/findings.py cmd_add computes `fid = _make_id(title, area)` (line 136) and then
gates on `if path.exists() and not args.force` (line 138). The path is derived from
the NEW title. So `--force` only overwrites when title+area are UNCHANGED.

Edit the title and pass --force and you do not replace anything: you mint a second
finding at a new id and leave the original in place. Nothing warns. The two records
then describe the same observation with slightly different titles, and only the author
knows one is stale.

The help text makes it worse rather than better: "--force  overwrite an existing
finding" (line 382). That is what the operator of the tool believes they are asking
for. What they get is an unconditional write at a possibly-different address.

CONSEQUENCE, already realised: CWNG KOBO filed F-c41b83, refined the title, re-ran
with --force, and got F-3b565b. Both existed simultaneously and untracked. They caught
it and deleted the stale one, but only because they happened to look — and had either
been committed first, the ledger would now carry a silent duplicate. The ledger's whole
premise per CLAUDE.md is that re-filing the same observation is "a no-op rather than a
duplicate", and this is the case where that premise quietly fails.

FIX OPTIONS, cheapest first:
1. Correct the help text to say what it does: "overwrite the finding with this exact
   title+area". One line, removes the misleading contract.
2. On --force, scan for near-duplicate titles in the same area before writing and warn
   with the candidate ids. The ledger already ships a `dedupe` subcommand that finds
   probable duplicate pairs, so the comparison logic exists.
3. Give `add` an explicit `--replace <id>` for "I mean THAT record", which is what a
   title edit actually intends.

NOT FILED AS A BUG AGAINST BEHAVIOUR SOMEONE RELIES ON: --force's current semantics are
fine for re-running the same add idempotently. The defect is that the one case a human
reaches for it — "I want to fix what I wrote" — is the case it does not serve.

Credit: CWNG KOBO, who filed it against their own careless tool use rather than the
tool. It is the tool.
title: findings.py --force keys on the title, so an edited title silently forks a second finding
